The charge cannot target buildings, which makes them poor at razing.

## Wootz Steel
Wootz Steel helps the Urumi less than other melee units, since its first hit already deals 30 damage. It only gives a real edge in long fights against heavily armored units such as Serjeants, Teutonic Knights and Boyars, and reaching critical mass is usually the better investment.

## What beats Urumi Swordsmen
Units that survive the first hit. Battle and War Elephants beat them with high HP and their own splash damage, and fully upgraded Konniks and Cataphracts win even in large fights. Other heavy cavalry wins when the Urumis lack numbers. Skirmishers deal them three times the damage they deal the Militia line and spread out while retreating, which limits the splash. Archers, Scorpions, Ballista Elephants and Monks also beat them. Organ Guns are exceptionally deadly, and other siege kills them quickly but dies just as quickly if the Urumis reach it.

villager.description:
The Villager is the economic unit of every civilization, trained at the Town Center from the Dark Age for 50 food in 25 seconds. Villagers gather food, wood, gold and stone, construct buildings and repair buildings, ships and siege weapons. Most civilizations start with three, the Chinese with six and the Maya with four.

With 25 HP, 3 attack and no armor, Villagers are poor fighters and stop working when attacked. They do have bonus damage against buildings and heavy siege, and garrisoned Villagers add arrows to the building they shelter in. Loom adds HP and armor, and the Spanish Supremacy technology makes them viable fighters in the early Imperial Age.
villager.tactics:
## Building an economy
A common guideline is to keep training Villagers until they make up half of the population limit, 100 under standard rules, and boom strategies go as high as 130. Gather rates differ by source: Pastures, fish and hunt are the fastest food, Farms and forage the slowest, and trees, gold and stone fall in between. Several Villagers build faster together, but each extra builder adds less than the first, so split them up unless a key building such as a Castle or Town Center must go up quickly.

Repairing a building or unit from 1 HP to full costs half its original cost, paid as the repair goes. The first Villager repairs 750 HP per minute on buildings and each extra one adds 375. Ships and siege repair at a quarter of that speed, and building something new is often faster than repairing it.

## Protecting Villagers
Against melee raiders, quickly placing building foundations around Villagers keeps attackers off them. Against ranged units, retreat or garrison. The Town Bell sends every Villager within 23 tiles into the nearest shelter, and Seek Shelter does the same for a selection. Each garrisoned Villager adds 2.5 garrison firepower, which in a Town Center or Fortified Church means one extra arrow per Villager.

## What beats Villagers
Almost every military unit. Villagers only hold their own against most buildings, rams, Trebuchets and small numbers of Skirmishers, so any raid that reaches them unprotected costs you economy.

war-chariot.description:
The second Shu unique unit, a cavalry siege unit that replaces the Scorpion line at the Siege Workshop from the Castle Age. It has no Elite upgrade. It costs 75 food and 90 gold and has 65 HP, 0/5 armor, a range of 6 and a minimum range of 1. It fires volleys of bolts and can switch between Focus Fire mode, where every bolt hits the target and passes through, and Barrage mode, which fires more bolts over a wider area.

It works like a mounted mix of Organ Gun and Scorpion. It handles archers, infantry and bunched units well, while cavalry and enemy siege beat it.
war-chariot.tactics:
## Fire modes and timing
In Focus Fire mode, fewer bolts all land on the target with pass-through damage, which works best against clustered archers. Barrage mode fires more bolts with wider spread, and bolts that hit other targets still deal full damage. The bolts go out one at a time, so more bolts means a longer reload. Bolt Magazine adds bolts in both modes at the cost of a slightly longer reload. Chemistry, Siege Engineers, Ballistics and the cavalry armor upgrades also apply.

War Chariots are often made in the early Castle Age: they need little food, come from the Siege Workshop and trade well against Feudal Age units. A few can catch an unprepared player off guard and badly damage the economy.

## Against archers and infantry
Most infantry cannot catch them. The barding armors make them very resistant to archers, and Composite Bowmen and Leiciai do not ignore their armor because they count as siege. Against Rattan Archers neither side does much, with a slight edge to the War Chariot from pass-through damage. Camel Archers are not effective, since War Chariots lack the cavalry archer armor class.

## What beats War Chariots
Enemy siege is the biggest threat, especially Mangonels and Bombard Cannons, which outrange them and hit the heavy siege class. Cavalry exploits the minimum range and lack of melee armor: Camel Riders are particularly dangerous, Magyar Huszars are cheap with an anti-siege bonus, Shrivamsha Riders dodge many bolts, and massed Light Cavalry also works. Eagle Warriors and Champi Warriors are fast with high pierce armor and bonus damage, and Genoese Crossbowmen are extremely deadly. Huskarls and Ghulams take little damage. Monks work if melee units or walls protect them.

war-elephant.description:
The Persian unique unit, a slow and very powerful cavalry unit trained at the Castle from the Castle Age and upgraded to the Elite War Elephant in the Imperial Age for 1,350 food and 800 gold. At 170 food and 85 gold it is one of the most expensive units in the game, and it takes 25 seconds to train.

It has 450 HP (600 as Elite), 15 attack (20 as Elite), +30 against buildings, and trample damage that hits nearby units for 50%. That makes it the most population-efficient unit in the game. At 0.8 speed it has trouble forcing fights, and Monks, Pikemen and siege weapons can bring it down.
war-elephant.tactics:
## Pitched battles
Fully upgraded, a War Elephant has 620 HP, more than three times a Paladin's, and 24 melee attack on top of its trample damage. It is one of the most situational unique units: if the specific units that counter it are dealt with, War Elephants are virtually unbeatable, and their durability makes them excellent in pitched battles and at knocking down buildings and defenses, which can do little against them. Their slow speed means even infantry can run away from them. The Persians have no Heresy, so War Elephants should always go out with ranged units or Light Cavalry to deal with enemy Monks.

## What beats War Elephants
Pikemen defeat them cost-efficiently, although it takes a large group, and Kamayuks also trade well. Mamelukes have the speed and anti-cavalry bonus to fight them. Cavalry Archers can kite them, though the elephants' HP and pierce armor mean it takes a while. Siege works because elephants are big, slow and melee only: Scorpions deal +6 bonus damage (+8 for Heavy Scorpions), and Mangonel shots are hard for them to dodge. The elephants are durable enough to reach the siege sometimes, so the siege should be backed by Pikemen. Monks can convert them. Flaming Camels deal 200 damage to elephant units before armor and are extremely lethal against packed groups. Genoese Crossbowmen are also strong against them.

war-galley.description:
The Castle Age upgrade of the Galley, trained at the Dock by every civilization for 90 wood and 30 gold. It later upgrades to the Galleon for 400 wood and 315 gold. Instead of arrows it fires large bolts, but each bolt only damages the single target it hits.

The Galley line is the backbone of any navy. War Galleys are cost-effective against Cannon Galleons, Demolition Ships and Transport Ships, and useful against units and buildings on the shoreline. Fire Ships are their main counter, and towers, Castles and siege on the shore outgun them.
war-galley.tactics:
## Getting the upgrade early
Compared to the Galley, the War Galley has 15 more HP, 1 more attack, 1 more range and trains 9 seconds faster. In naval battles, a quick Castle Age with the War Galley upgrade, along with upgrades for the other Feudal warships, is considered essential. The Fletching, Bodkin Arrow and Bracer line adds attack and range, Ballistics lets the bolts hit moving targets, and Careening and Dry Dock add pierce armor.

## Using War Galleys
They work much better in large numbers and should be paired with Fire Ships in most cases. With good micro they deal cost-effectively with Cannon Galleons and Demolition Ships. Demolition Ships die quickly to their fire but still do enough damage to be a threat. War Galleys are also excellent escorts for Transport Ships and good at picking off Fishing Ships. Against shoreline targets they are useful except against towers, Castles and siege units.

## What beats War Galleys
Fire Ships are their main counter, though War Galleys in large enough numbers can hold their own, especially alongside Demolition Ships or Hulks. Turtle Ships and Longships beat them, and War Hulks win at close distance while losing at long range. Towers, Castles and ranged siege units on the shoreline also outgun them.

war-wagon.description:
The first Korean unique unit, a mounted archer trained at the Castle from the Castle Age and upgraded to Elite War Wagon in the Imperial Age. It costs 100 wood and 60 gold and has 150 HP, 9 attack, range 4 and very high pierce armor. It fires bolts like a War Galley, without pass-through damage.

War Wagons play like bulkier, faster Arbalesters and can be ranged support, a meat shield, or both at once. They are strong against infantry, archers and buildings and can shoot Villagers from inside Town Center range. Melee cavalry, camels, fast infantry with high pierce armor, Monks and ranged siege beat them.
war-wagon.tactics:
## Holding the line
War Wagons are too slow and fire too slowly for hit and run. They work like Elephant Archers, as durable ranged units that hold an area or push. As support they sit behind Halberdiers. As a front line they can lead Rocket Carts and Bombard Cannons, and the ranged attack lets them hit enemies without chasing them and breaking formation. They also raid well, destroy buildings quickly with their bonus, and on maps with narrow paths such as Black Forest their large size can block the way and buy time.

The big collision box makes micro hard even in small groups, and in large groups it cuts into how many can reach their range. Upgrades are limited to the archer attack line, Thumb Ring, Ballistics and Husbandry.

## What beats War Wagons
Halberdiers and Camel Riders, which they should not face head on. Paladins, War Elephants and Battle Elephants overpower them, though the elephants struggle to force a fight. Ghulams, Eagle Warriors and Huskarls cut them down with high pierce armor and strong attacks. War Wagons lack Heresy, and their high cost makes them prime targets for Monks. Camel Archers lose one on one but are much cheaper and deal bonus damage. Elite Skirmishers need large numbers to win. Onagers, Bombard Cannons and even Trebuchets hit the clumsy wagons hard; Korean Bombard Cannons are the answer to enemy siege.

warrior-priest.description:
The Warrior Priest is the Armenian unique infantry unit, trained at the Fortified Church from the Castle Age. It is a hybrid of a Two-Handed Swordsman and a Monk: it heals friendly units and carries Relics, but it cannot convert. It costs 40 food and 50 gold and has 80 HP, 11 attack and 1/1 armor. Converting it requires Atonement, and it has no Elite upgrade.

It fights well against most melee infantry and holds up against foot archers. As a religious unit it takes anti-Monk bonus damage, so Light Cavalry and Eagle Warriors beat it.
warrior-priest.tactics:
## Healing
Warrior Priests heal 2 HP per second from 4 tiles, 80% of a Monk's rate. Fereters doubles that to 4 HP per second, faster than a Monk, and a Byzantine ally doubles it again. Keep a few close to the army on Stand Ground or No Attack stance so they heal instead of fighting. They do this job better than Monks, since archers and scouts cannot snipe them easily and they can defend themselves.

## Relics
Warrior Priests should be the ones to pick up Relics. They move faster than Monks, train 70% faster and can kill enemy Monks, which will usually lack Atonement in the early Castle Age. Enemy scouts deal bonus damage to religious units and may win that fight, depending on technologies. The one drawback is line of sight, capped at 7 against a Monk's 11.

## In combat
They start out fairly strong for Castle Age infantry. Sanctity adds +15 HP and Fereters +30, Fervor raises their speed to 0.98 and Squires adds another 10%. They have no attack bonuses, though Arson gives +2 against standard buildings. High HP and decent speed after the Fortified Church technologies let them soak arrows and chase down foot archers.

## What beats Warrior Priests
Light Cavalry and, even more so, Eagle Warriors, which deal anti-Monk bonus damage. Hand Cannoneers and Slingers stay very effective against them, and Plumed Archers and mounted archers are fast enough to shoot them down. Samurai, Jaguar Warriors, Teutonic Knights, Urumi Swordsmen and heavy cavalry also beat them.

winged-hussar.description:
The Winged Hussar is a light cavalry unit that the Lithuanians and Poles get by upgrading the Light Cavalry at the Stable in the Imperial Age. It replaces the Hussar upgrade for those two civilizations and has no Elite version. The upgrade costs 600 food and 800 gold, or 300 food and 800 gold for the Poles.

It costs 80 food and has 80 HP, 9 attack and 1/2 armor, more HP, attack and melee armor than a Hussar. It is fast, resists conversion and has +14 attack against Monks and +4 against gunpowder units. As a food only trash unit it is good against archers, siege, Monks and gunpowder units, and weak against most melee units.
winged-hussar.tactics:
## Using Winged Hussars
Winged Hussars attack every 1.9 seconds, and even without Bloodlines one beats a Light Cavalry that has it. They are useful for harassing small towns and armies before they grow, stopping small siege attacks and running down small groups of archers. When gold runs low they are the main cavalry of the Poles and Lithuanians. Among trash units they beat Elite Skirmishers and lose to Halberdiers, and their bonus helps against gunpowder units.

## Poles and Lithuanians
Polish Winged Hussars get +1 attack against archers from the Polish team bonus, Blast Furnace for melee fights and blast damage from Lechitic Legacy, which makes them strong in big fights. They lack Plate Barding Armor, so arrows hurt them more. Lithuanian ones lack Blast Furnace but have Plate Barding Armor and Heresy, which makes them sturdier against archers and Monks.

Lithuanians can pair them with Cavalry Archers, since the archers spend wood and gold while the Hussars spend only food, though they lack Parthian Tactics. This works less well for the Poles. Poles can mix in Arbalesters and Lithuanians Hand Cannoneers to pick off Halberdiers, at the cost of a slower army.

## What beats Winged Hussars
Halberdiers are the standard answer, the trash unit built to counter light cavalry. Most other melee units also beat them in a straight fight. Genoese Crossbowmen, with their bonus against cavalry, also beat them.

woad-raider.description:
The Celtic unique infantry, trained at the Castle from the Castle Age, with an Elite upgrade in the Imperial Age. It costs 70 food and 25 gold, trains in 10 seconds and has 70 HP (85 as Elite), 11 attack (15 as Elite) and a bonus against Standard Buildings. The Celtic bonus makes it 15% faster in the Castle Age and 20% faster in the Imperial Age.

It is the second fastest infantry in the game after Elite Eagle Warriors with Squires, which makes it a strong raider. It beats most infantry and siege, but heavy cavalry, massed archers and stronger unique infantry beat it.
woad-raider.tactics:
## Raiding and fighting
Speed fixes the usual infantry problem of not being able to force fights, and the Celts have few other fast options. The standard Woad Raider is close to a Long Swordsman and the Elite one to a Champion: it costs more food and slightly more gold, but has more HP and attack and trains in half the time. It has 0 melee armor where the Militia line has 1. Arson adds damage against buildings, and the Blacksmith attack and infantry armor upgrades apply.

Its attack and HP let it hold its own against most infantry, and it beats Elite Skirmishers, Halberdiers, Eagle Warriors and Light Cavalry. It is also good against siege weapons and useful for killing Trebuchets that come too close.

## What beats Woad Raiders
Heavy cavalry such as Knights, Cataphracts and Boyars, along with Battle Elephants and War Elephants. Massed archers shoot them down. Stronger unique infantry such as Teutonic Knights, Samurai, Jaguar Warriors, Obuchs, Berserks, Urumi Swordsmen and Legionaries win the melee fight.

xolotl-warrior.description:
A heavy cavalry unit of the American civilizations (Aztecs, Inca, Mapuche, Maya, Muisca and Tupi), trained at the Stable from the Castle Age with the same statistics as the Knight. In regular games it is trained from a Stable taken from the enemy: with Redemption, the Aztecs, Inca, Muisca and Tupi can convert an enemy Stable; the Maya and Mapuche lack Redemption and cannot.

All six can also train it from Stables placed in the Scenario Editor, starting Stables on some MegaRandom maps, or Stables captured in Battle Royale. It costs 60 food and 75 gold and has 100 HP, 10 attack and 2/2 armor.
xolotl-warrior.tactics:
## Using Xolotl Warriors
Like the Knight, the Xolotl Warrior is a powerful and versatile addition to almost any army. High attack and speed make it good for assaults and flanking, and its HP and armor make it a meat shield for ranged units and siege on the front line. The American civilizations get no Cavalier upgrade, no Blacksmith armor technologies, no Bloodlines and no Husbandry for it, so the unit falls behind badly in the late Castle Age and the Imperial Age.

## Post-Imperial starts
In games that start in the Post-Imperial Age, such as Deathmatch and Battle Royale, the unit begins with +30 HP, +2 attack and +2/+2 armor. That puts it almost level with a Viking Cavalier, with a 10 HP advantage, though still behind a fully upgraded generic Cavalier by 10 HP, 1/2 armor and 0.14 speed. Advancing to the Imperial Age during a game does not give this bonus; only Post-Imperial starts do.

## What beats Xolotl Warriors
It shares the Knight's weaknesses. Pikemen and Camel Riders hard counter it, and Monks can convert it. Other heavy cavalry, archers, Kamayuks, Berserks, Teutonic Knights and Mamelukes also beat it, especially since it cannot be upgraded. It does well against infantry, siege weapons and light cavalry.

blackwood-archer.description:
The first Tupi unique unit, a foot archer trained in pairs at the Castle in the Castle Age. A pair costs 40 wood and 45 gold, and each archer takes only half a population slot and refunds 15% of its cost when killed. It can be upgraded to Elite Blackwood Archer in the Imperial Age.

Individually it is very weak, with 20 HP, the lowest of any regular unit, and 4 pierce attack. A fast rate of fire, decent speed and sheer numbers make up for it. Blackwood Archers are good against Spearmen, infantry and other archers, and they lose to skirmishers, heavy cavalry and splash damage.
blackwood-archer.tactics:
## Mass them first
Blackwood Archers die easily in small numbers, so they should be massed before they join a fight. Their fast attack helps against units with high pierce armor such as Huskarls. Their bonus damage beats Pikemen and Halberdiers, and their speed lets them kite slow infantry. Against other archers they usually win through numbers, because enemy archers overkill and waste shots, and the Tupi get part of the cost of their losses back.

## Upgrades
The Elite upgrade adds 5 HP, a little accuracy and cuts training time by 4 seconds. Against splash damage the extra HP rarely matters, but it lets them survive one more hit from units such as the Elite Huskarl. Curare adds poison that ignores armor and stacks across archers, which makes them deadlier than other archers against Paladins, Rattan Archers, Huskarls, Ghulams and Tiger Cavalry. It can overkill a target that is already dying and does not affect siege, ships or buildings. With a Saracen ally they get bonus damage against buildings and can tear down weaker ones, though Castles and Keeps are still off limits.

## What beats Blackwood Archers
Elite Skirmishers and Genitours slaughter them. Heavy cavalry wins easily, Knights even against good micro, and Light Cavalry is reasonably cost-effective too. Mangonels, Scorpions and anything else with splash damage are terrible for them. Rattan Archers, War Wagons and Elephant Archers have enough pierce armor or HP to make them very ineffective.

bolas-rider.description:
The second Mapuche unique unit, a short ranged anti-cavalry mounted archer trained at the Archery Range from the Castle Age and upgraded to Elite Bolas Rider in the Imperial Age. It costs 50 wood and 55 gold and has 55 HP, 5 attack, range 4 and bonus damage against cavalry, camels and rams.

Every 30 seconds it throws a charged shot with +2 attack (+3 Elite) that slows the target by 15% for 10 seconds, so slower units can catch what it hits. It is good against mounted units and infantry. It has less HP than a Cavalry Archer and no Thumb Ring or Parthian Tactics, and Skirmishers, ranged siege and Shrivamsha Riders beat it.
bolas-rider.tactics:
## Using the slow
The slow does not stack, so when several Bolas Riders shoot the same target the effect is wasted. Use attack move or patrol against medium and large armies so each rider picks a different target, especially when they support foot archers or infantry. Bolas Riders can also raid and hit and run like Cavalry Archers, with gold returned for each military unit killed. After the first charged shot their damage is lower than a Cavalry Archer's, especially against high pierce armor units like Eagle Warriors.

Malon gives their attack 30% pass-through damage, and with it every enemy hit by the charged shot is slowed. That makes large groups a real threat to cavalry blobs and helps against clumped foot archers. They pair well with the rest of the Mapuche army, letting Barracks and Archery Range units force fights against faster units, and with the Kona for raiding. A Fast Castle into a Bolas Rider rush is an option, and Butalmapu cuts their cost by 15%.

## What beats Bolas Riders
Skirmishers, and Genitours, which take bonus damage from them but are still cost effective. Genoese Crossbowmen and Rattan Archers, and massed foot archers such as Arbalesters, which outrange them. Other mounted archers: Camel Archers, Japanese Cavalry Archers, Ballista Elephants and Elephant Archers. Mangonels and Scorpions, since the charged shot is not used on siege. Shrivamsha Riders absorb the charged shot and the slow. Cataphracts negate the bonus damage, and Camel Riders, Mamelukes, Savars and Tiger Cavalry are dangerous at close range.

camel-scout.description:
The Camel Scout is one of the three unique units of the Gurjaras and their unique scout unit. They start the game with one, and from the Feudal Age they can train more at the Stable for 55 food and 60 gold. It has 70 HP and no armor. There is no Elite version, and on reaching the Castle Age every Camel Scout becomes a Camel Rider automatically.

In the Dark Age it is a scout with only 2 attack. In the Feudal Age it gains attack, speed and line of sight, plus +5 against cavalry, which makes it strong against Scout Cavalry and Skirmishers. Spearmen and defensive structures beat it.
camel-scout.tactics:
## Dark Age scouting
In the Dark Age the Camel Scout's attack is too weak for fighting, so it scouts, collects Sheep and other herdables and finds gold and stone. It has the same speed and line of sight as Scout Cavalry and kills Boars in the same number of hits. Town Centers need only 12 arrows to kill it, considerably fewer than for other scouts, and with no attack bonuses it is useless for killing enemy herdables. Its one edge over Scout Cavalry is that it always wins an even duel. All Camel Scouts have a toggleable Auto Scout ability, and they cannot attack timid huntables such as Deer.

## Feudal Age anti-cavalry
Reaching the Feudal Age gives every Camel Scout +2 attack, +1 line of sight, +0.25 speed and +5 attack against cavalry, which turns it into an anti-cavalry unit that fends off enemy Scout Cavalry. In team games it is a very good early Feudal Age unit that can kill two Scout Cavalry back to back, and a strong defensive tool for the whole team. Fast and with high HP, it also counters Skirmishers. It is hard to mass, since it takes longer to train and needs both a good food and a good gold economy.

## What beats Camel Scouts
Spearmen, which kill camels as easily as other mounted units. Archers also do well against them, though Feudal Age Archers are less of a threat than Castle Age Crossbowmen. Defensive structures are a problem too, with a Town Center needing just 12 arrows to bring one down.

champi-runner.description:
The Champi Runner is an infantry scout unit upgraded from the Champi Scout at the Barracks in the Feudal Age. It is a regional unit of the Inca, Mapuche, Muisca and Tupi, and it upgrades further to the Champi Warrior. It can build Outposts.

It costs 50 food and 25 gold and has 40 HP, 5 attack, 2 pierce armor and a speed of 1.10. It fills a role close to the Man-at-Arms but raids like an Eagle Scout: it is fast, sees far and holds up better than the Militia line against arrows. It loses to the Militia line, heavy infantry and heavy cavalry.
champi-runner.tactics:
## Feudal Age raids
The Champi Runner has 1 more attack than the Champi Scout, which helps against Villagers and buildings, and the upgrade is cheap enough to be almost always worth it, especially against Eagle Scouts. A good raiding party is about a dozen Champi Runners with some Skirmishers against enemy archers, plus Spearmen if the enemy has a lot of Scout Cavalry. Mixing in your own archers improves the raid further. Murder Holes is not available in the Feudal Age, so they can zig-zag to the base of a tower where it cannot shoot them. Against Scout Cavalry they do fairly well but die quickly when outnumbered.

Upgrade them quickly when moving into the Castle Age, since the enemy then gets many more counters. The Champi Scout line costs more to upgrade than the Militia line but has four upgrades to its five.

## Civilization differences
Inca Champi Runners cost 20% less food in the Feudal Age. Mapuche ones have +5 HP, the same as a Man-at-Arms. Muisca ones get +1 melee armor but lack Arson, and their Settlements heal them. Tupi ones return 15% of their cost when they die.

## What beats Champi Runners
The Militia line, which has more HP and attack and wins in melee. Heavy infantry and heavy cavalry also beat them. Archers are worth avoiding even though Champi Runners resist them better than the Militia line, and large groups of Scout Cavalry can mob them.

champi-scout.description:
An infantry scout trained at the Barracks from the Dark Age, available only to the Inca, Mapuche, Muisca and Tupi. These civilizations start the game with one in place of a mounted scout. It costs 50 food and 25 gold and has 35 HP, 3 attack, 2 pierce armor and bonuses against cavalry, camels, shock infantry and siege. It can build Outposts and upgrades to the Champi Runner.

It is a fast generalist that resists arrows. Compared with the Militia it has more pierce armor, speed and line of sight but less HP, so heavy infantry and heavy cavalry beat it.
champi-scout.tactics:
## Scouting and the Dark Age rush
As a starting scout it is comparable to an Eagle Scout in speed and line of sight, and unlike the Militia or Eagle Scout it can build Outposts. A Champi Scout drush sends a small band into the enemy base to harass, disrupt the economy and often stop early walling, with your own scout blocking fleeing Villagers that are low on HP. Villagers without Loom fall quickly, but Villagers with Loom can win if they strike first or garrison in the Town Center. The usual goal is to delay enemy walls or buy time for your own. A higher gold cost and a 42 second training time make this a little harder than a Militia rush. When going for disruption, follow up with a fast Feudal Age and the Champi Runner upgrade, which kills Villagers, scouts and walls faster.

## Differences by civilization
Inca Champi Scouts cost 15% less food in the Dark Age, and the Inca also pay less stone for Outposts. Mapuche ones are the most generic in the Dark Age, as their bonuses come later. Muisca ones can retreat to a Settlement to heal 5 HP per minute. Tupi ones return 15% of their cost when they die, so a failed drush loses less, and the Champi Runner upgrade costs the Tupi half the food.

## What beats Champi Scouts
Heavy infantry and heavy cavalry, since the Champi Scout has little HP and attack for melee fights. In the Dark Age, Villagers with Loom can beat a small group, especially when garrisoning in the Town Center is an option.

champi-warrior.description:
The Castle Age infantry scout of the Inca, Mapuche, Muisca and Tupi, upgraded from the Champi Runner at the Barracks and upgraded again to the Elite Champi Warrior for 650 food and 450 gold. It costs 50 food and 25 gold, and like its predecessor it can build Outposts.

It has 55 HP, 9 attack and 3 pierce armor, with bonuses against siege weapons and buildings, and it is faster than a Long Swordsman. It fills a similar slot to the Long Swordsman with Eagle Warrior traits, which makes it a good raider that resists arrows. It is weak against heavy cavalry, most other infantry and Monks.
champi-warrior.tactics:
## A raiding generalist
The upgrade from the Champi Runner gives +15 HP, +4 attack, +1 against siege and buildings and +1 pierce armor, and is worth getting quickly if the line sees any real use. Champi Warriors are the basic Castle Age infantry of the South American civilizations and the best raiders for the Muisca, Inca and Tupi. One on one they beat standard Castle Age units except the Knight, Cavalry Archer and Long Swordsman, and they do well against Pikemen, Light Cavalry, Camel Riders, Elite Skirmishers, Eagle Warriors, most siege and most archers. They are also the answer to shock infantry and low melee armor units like Huskarls. Support them with Slingers against Monks and infantry, Pikemen against cavalry, and Skirmishers or Mangonels against archers.

## Civilization differences
Inca Champi Warriors cost 25% less food in the Castle Age and pair well with Kamayuks, which handle heavy cavalry. Mapuche ones have +10 HP but lack Squires and work best as basic infantry against trash units. Muisca ones have +2 melee armor in the Castle Age, lack Arson, heal at Settlements, and with Herbalism are the best raiders of all. Tupi Champi Warriors return 15% of their cost on death, attack faster with Caciques, which makes them a hard counter to siege, and their upgrades cost 50% less food.

## What beats Champi Warriors
Heavy infantry and heavy cavalry, along with most other infantry. Monks can convert them, and their low HP leaves them fragile once they are caught.

dragon-ship.description:
The Chinese unique upgrade of the Fire Ship, available at the Dock in the Imperial Age once Heavy Warships is researched. It replaces the Fast Fire Ship for the Chinese and costs 75 wood and 45 gold. Like other fire ships it sprays fire from a flamethrower on the bow and has to get very close to enemy ships to attack.

It has 5 fewer HP than a Fast Fire Ship but 1 more attack, 0.5 more range and, with the Chinese Fire Ship speed bonus, a speed of 1.72 against 1.56. It is strong against Galleons and Cannon Galleons and weak against Demolition Ships and Carracks.
dragon-ship.tactics:
## Front line of the fleet
The Dragon Ship is in most respects better than the Fast Fire Ship. It works as a durable front line vessel that soaks up shots from enemy Galleons and ties up enemy Fast Fire Ships. Its extra speed makes it better at chasing ships down and at escaping fights that go badly, and its flames track moving targets on their own. It trains in 27 seconds, the same as a Fire Ship. It is also good against Transport Ships, Fishing Ships, buildings on the shoreline and melee units in the shallows. Siphons gives it an explosive charge attack, and Careening, Dry Dock and Shipwright improve it as they do other ships.

## What beats Dragon Ships
Massed Galleons can focus them down, especially with good micro. Demolition Ships are strong against them, and Carracks, Turtle Ships and Longships beat them too. Towers, Castles and ranged siege on the shoreline also keep them away from the coast.

elite-champi-warrior.description:
A fast, archer-resistant infantry scout upgraded from the Champi Warrior at the Barracks once the Imperial Age is reached, for 650 food and 450 gold. It is a regional unit for the Inca, Mapuche, Muisca and Tupi, and their basic infantry in the Imperial Age. It costs 50 food and 25 gold and has 65 HP, 11 attack, 0/4 armor and a speed of 1.1.

It can build Outposts and has bonus damage against siege and buildings. It is good against trash units, siege, shock infantry and archers, and for the Inca, Muisca and Tupi it is the best raider. Heavy cavalry, most other infantry and Monks beat it.
elite-champi-warrior.tactics:
## Upgrade and support
The Elite upgrade adds +10 HP, +2 attack, +1 attack against buildings and +1 pierce armor. Against an opponent massing trash units or archers it is a must. Elite Champi Warriors are comparable to Two-Handed Swordsmen but lose to them because of lower attack and melee armor, the Mapuche version excepted, and all of them lose to Champions. Support them with Slingers against infantry and Monks, Pikemen against cavalry, and Skirmishers or Mangonels against archers. They are also the South American answer to units with low melee armor such as Gothic Huskarls.

## Differences between civilizations
Inca Champis cost less food, get Fabric Shields for +1/+1 armor and pair well with Kamayuks. Mapuche Champis have +15 HP, more than a generic Champion, but no Squires, which makes them the slowest. They work best as basic infantry against trash. Muisca Champis have +3 melee armor in the Imperial Age but no Arson or Blast Furnace, heal at Settlements, and with Herbalism are the best raiders. Tupi Champis refund 15% of their cost on death, attack faster with Caciques and become a hard counter to siege.

## What beats Elite Champi Warriors
Heavy cavalry, which they have no answer to without Pikemen nearby. Heavy infantry such as Champions, and Two-Handed Swordsmen in most cases, win because the Champi has no base melee armor. Monks can also convert them.

elite-fire-lancer.description:
The Elite Fire Lancer is the Imperial Age upgrade of the Fire Lancer at the Barracks, a regional unit of the Chinese, Jurchens, Khitans, Koreans and Vietnamese. It is gunpowder shock infantry and the only infantry in the game that costs no food: 45 wood and 45 gold. It has 85 HP, 10 attack, 2/1 armor and +15 bonus damage against cavalry and elephants.

When fighting units it fires a volley of three projectiles at range 5, each dealing 4 damage that ignores armor, and the volley recharges every 30 seconds. It is good against cavalry and Skirmishers and weak against other infantry.
elite-fire-lancer.tactics:
## Using the volley
The charged volley works best against masses of units, especially slow ones such as other infantry. With proper micromanagement and hit-and-run tactics, Elite Fire Lancers can counter infantry like Teutonic Knights. They should avoid direct fights with heavy infantry, which has a large bonus against them, as well as Condottieri and units with bonuses against infantry, such as Hand Cannoneers. In melee they counter cavalry well, although Halberdiers are much better at that job. Supported by units that cover their weaknesses, they can deal with most army compositions.

## Civilization differences
Chinese Elite Fire Lancers move 10% faster and their technologies cost 15% less, but they lack Gambesons, and Chu Ko Nu and Rocket Carts make good partners. Jurchen ones attack 25% faster and are the strongest in melee. They lack Plate Mail Armor and pair well with Iron Pagodas. Khitan ones get double Blacksmith attack upgrades and reflect 25% melee damage with Lamellar Armor, which makes them the most well-rounded. Korean ones cost 50% less wood but lack Blast Furnace and are the weakest in melee. Vietnamese ones also lack Blast Furnace but get free Conscription.

## What beats Elite Fire Lancers
Infantry in general, and heavy infantry above all, because of its large bonus damage. Condottieri deal bonus damage to gunpowder units, and Hand Cannoneers deal bonus damage to infantry. Ranged units are a bigger problem for Chinese and Jurchen Fire Lancers, which lack Gambesons and Plate Mail Armor respectively.

elite-varangian-guard.description:
The Elite Varangian Guard is the Imperial Age upgrade of the Varangian Guard, trained at the Barracks. It is a regional unit of the Byzantines, Danes, Saxons, Varangians and Vikings. The upgrade costs 750 food and 475 gold.

It is a generalist shock infantry unit that generates 42 gold per minute while attacking enemy units. It costs 65 food and 45 gold and has 80 HP, 17 attack and 2/2 armor. Compared with a Champion it has more HP, attack and armor and moves faster, but costs more, trains slower and has no bonus damage. It does well against cavalry, Elite Skirmishers, Halberdiers and buildings.
elite-varangian-guard.tactics:
## Civilization differences
The Byzantines and Saxons lack Blast Furnace, so their Elite Varangian Guards have 2 less attack. Byzantines get trample damage from Logistica. Saxon ones become up to 20% cheaper with more Town Centers and Castles and gain up to +3/+3 armor from Shield Wall when 15 other infantry are nearby. Danish ones move 10% faster and get extra attack from Hamask as they lose HP. Varangian ones attack 25% faster, generate 50% more gold and get a ranged charge attack from Gothikon. Viking ones have 20% more HP and +5 attack against cavalry from Chieftains, but lack Gambesons.

The usual infantry technologies apply: the Blacksmith attack and armor upgrades, Gambesons, Squires, Arson against buildings and Conscription.

## What beats Elite Varangian Guards
The Militia line, because Champions and their predecessors deal bonus damage to shock infantry. Foot archers and Elite Champi Warriors also counter them.

fire-archer.description:
The first Wu unique unit, a foot archer trained at the Castle from the Castle Age, with an Elite upgrade in the Imperial Age. It costs 45 wood and 45 gold and has 35 HP (40 as Elite). Against buildings and ships it switches automatically to a single long range shot with a range of 9 (10 as Elite) and a bonus against Standard Buildings and ships. Against units it fires three arrows in a row at a range of 5 (6 as Elite), each with a small area effect that does not hurt friendly units.

It is built for sieging and ship fighting and is weaker in regular combat. Cavalry, Skirmishers and siege weapons beat it.
fire-archer.tactics:
## Sieging in the Castle Age
Fire Archers are the only Castle Age unit that outranges even upgraded Castles and towers. With their bonus against buildings and the Wu unique technology Red Cliffs Tactics, which adds damage over time in the anti-building mode, they let the Wu siege down fortifications in the Castle Age from relative safety. They can still do this in the Imperial Age, but Trebuchets and other siege make it less important there. Fletching, Bodkin Arrow and Bracer add attack and range, and Ballistics lets them track moving targets.

## In regular combat
The anti-unit attack is a short range volley released one arrow after another, like a Chu Ko Nu. It is less efficient than a standard archer, and Fire Archers do much worse than the same number of Crossbowmen or Arbalesters in most fights. They do well against slow, weak melee units, especially Spearmen, and against siege weapons and ships at close range.

## What beats Fire Archers
Other archers, especially Elite Skirmishers. Cavalry, Huskarls and Eagle Warriors close in and kill them, and siege weapons also beat them.

fire-lancer.description:
A gunpowder infantry unit trained at the Barracks from the Castle Age by the Chinese, Jurchens, Khitans, Koreans and Vietnamese, and upgraded to the Elite Fire Lancer in the Imperial Age for 750 food and 400 gold. It costs 45 wood and 45 gold.

It fills the anti-cavalry role of the Pikeman, with 65 HP, 9 attack and bonuses against cavalry, elephants and camels. Every 30 seconds it can open a fight with a volley of three projectiles at range 4 that ignore armor. Archers, Hand Cannoneers, Long Swordsmen and anti-gunpowder units such as Condottieri counter it, and it costs gold and trains slowly.
fire-lancer.tactics:
## The charged attack
When fighting units other than siege, a Fire Lancer fires three inaccurate projectiles at a range of 4, each dealing 3 pierce damage that ignores armor, so the volley works best against groups. It recharges in 30 seconds and does not fire while the unit is in melee. In practice it gives one strong hit before melee begins, which helps most against high armor targets like heavy cavalry. Together with its anti-cavalry bonus and solid stats, this can make it better than Pikemen against the Knight line, especially in population efficiency, though Pikemen are more cost-efficient when gold is short.

## Role and economy
Unlike Pikemen, Fire Lancers take no bonus damage from archers and gain pierce armor from Gambesons, so they are more resilient. Their attack and HP also give them some raiding potential. They cost gold and take 10 seconds longer to train, so they are less disposable and harder to mass on defense. Many Fire Lancer civilizations focus on archers (Chinese, Koreans, Vietnamese) or siege (Jurchens), so their economies already run on wood and gold and can make Fire Lancers against enemy cavalry and Skirmishers without shifting to food. They also beat the Spearman line at equal resources, which makes them a good all-round counter to trash units.

## What beats Fire Lancers
Archers and especially Hand Cannoneers counter them in most cases. As shock infantry they lose to Long Swordsmen and various unique infantry units. They take bonus damage from anti-gunpowder attacks, which makes them especially weak against Condottieri and Konas. They still beat Winged Hussars at equal resources.

flaming-camel.description:
The second Tatar unique unit, a mounted suicide unit trained at the Siege Workshop in the Imperial Age for 75 food and 30 gold. It works like a mounted Petard: when it attacks or dies it explodes and deals melee damage to all enemies nearby. It has no Elite upgrade.

Its explosion carries large bonuses against elephants, cavalry, camels and buildings, which makes it one of the best answers to packed groups of elephant units. It has 55 HP and no armor of any kind, and nothing can raise its armor, so ranged units kill it quickly. Against buildings it is much weaker than a Petard.
flaming-camel.tactics:
## Blowing up mounted armies
Flaming Camels are best used against large groups of mounted units. Their bonus damage kills most mounted units in two or three blasts while the splash hits everything around the target. Against packed War Elephants, Battle Elephants, Ballista Elephants, Elephant Archers and Siege Elephants each blast deals at least 200 damage, so they are a strong pick against any civilization with elephants. Heavy Camel Riders should follow up to finish the units that survive.

They are mounted units but not cavalry, so Forging, Scale Barding Armor and Silk Armor do nothing for them. Only Devotion, Husbandry, Bloodlines and Siege Engineers affect them. Husbandry is worth getting: the extra speed helps them reach big groups of Cavalry Archers and avoid fire from Castles.

## Against buildings
A Flaming Camel does only 40% of a Petard's damage to buildings while costing more, so it is not cost-effective there. A Keep takes 4 Petards or 10 Flaming Camels, and against walls and gates the gap is even larger. It is a support unit for weakening or finishing a town, or for a surprise attack.

## What beats Flaming Camels
Foot archers and other ranged units shoot them down before they arrive, since they have no pierce armor. Pikemen and Elite Skirmishers are cost-effective against them, and Monks, infantry in general and defensive structures also do well. Mounted archers can counter them, unless they bunch up and let the camels reach them.

grenadier.description:
The second Jurchen unique unit, a gunpowder foot archer trained at the Archery Range from the Castle Age, with no Elite upgrade. It costs 55 food and 50 gold and has 40 HP, 12 attack with +9 against infantry, range 6 and a minimum range of 1. It throws explosive iron balls that deal splash damage, much like a Mangonel on foot with low accuracy and no attack ground.

Grenadiers are a Castle Age alternative to the Hand Cannoneer, far better against groups of infantry and weaker against single targets. Their shots cause friendly fire, halved for Jurchen units. They need protection and large numbers, and cavalry, Elite Skirmishers and siege beat them.
grenadier.tactics:
## Massing and Thunderclap Bombs
With very low accuracy and a slow attack, Grenadiers only work in numbers and must be kept behind other units, since their low HP leads to costly losses. Thunderclap Bombs is the most important upgrade, since there is no Elite version: projectiles detonate some time after landing and Grenadiers explode when they die, which raises their damage and makes it risky to fight them in melee. The Jurchens get Siege Engineers in the Castle Age at a discount for +1 range, and Ballistics improves their aim against moving units. They cover the weakness to infantry of Iron Pagodas, Halberdiers and Fire Lancers, and Hussars with Bombard Cannons round out a strong army.

## Against archers
Crossbowmen and Elite Skirmishers outrange them once the Blacksmith upgrades are in. If Grenadiers get close, the splash wipes out clumped archers, so enemy archers need to keep their distance and wait for upgrades.

## What beats Grenadiers
Cavalry, Winged Hussars above all, which exploits their cost, low durability and minimum range. Rattan Archers and Genitours trade very well against them, and Elephant Archers and War Wagons are too durable to fight. Mangonels outrange them and kill them in one shot, and Scorpions are also very dangerous. Condottieri and Huskarls shrug off the damage and have bonuses against them, though a large, microed group can still win, especially with Thunderclap Bombs. Spread your units in a staggered formation to limit the splash.

guecha-warrior.description:
The Guecha Warrior is the Castle unique unit of the Muisca, a javelin-throwing foot archer trained at the Castle from the Castle Age. It costs 50 wood and 60 gold and works like an expensive Skirmisher that gives up some range and pierce armor for more HP, more speed and much more attack. It has 6 attack, range 3 and 3 pierce armor. The Elite Guecha Warrior in the Imperial Age, for 750 wood and 600 gold, has 8 attack, range 4 and 5 pierce armor.

When a Guecha Warrior dies, nearby Guecha Warriors regenerate some HP. It is strong against archers and slow infantry and weak against melee cavalry and anti-archer units.
guecha-warrior.tactics:
## An expensive Skirmisher
Guecha Warriors keep the Skirmisher's anti-archer role but hit every unit much harder, and their speed of 1.15 is the key to micromanaging them and picking fights. When one dies, the others within 6 tiles regenerate 5 HP over 3 seconds, so a large group is durable. Their range is shorter than an Elite Skirmisher's, which makes them worse against Crossbowmen in the Castle Age, though their speed partly makes up for that and helps them dodge Mangonel shots. Massed, they beat other infantry more easily than Crossbowmen do.

## Raiding like mounted archers
They can also take the role of mounted archers, hitting and running against slow infantry and raiding Villagers despite their slow rate of fire. Unlike Cavalry Archers they take no anti-cavalry bonus damage.

## What beats Guecha Warriors
The usual anti-archer units: Elite Skirmishers, Huskarls, Ghulams, Genitours, Eagle Warriors and Champi Warriors. Melee cavalry is a problem because of their slow attack, low melee armor and minimum range. A group of 36 Elite Guecha Warriors can kill a Paladin in one volley, where 60 Arbalesters would be needed, yet heavy cavalry still counters them, with Savars and Tiger Cavalry as notable threats. Bengali melee mounted units beat them thanks to bonus damage against skirmishers, and siege units are dangerous as well.

heavy-hei-guang-cavalry.description:
The Heavy Hei Guang Cavalry is the Imperial Age upgrade of the Hei Guang Cavalry, trained at the Stable by the Shu, Wei and Wu. Its description and role are the same as those of the Knight line: powerful all purpose heavy cavalry.

It costs 65 food and 65 gold and trains in 28 seconds. It has 90 HP, 12 attack, +1 against infantry and 4/3 armor, so it trades hit points for armor compared with the Knight line. It is strong against infantry, siege weapons and light cavalry, and weak against Halberdiers, Heavy Camel Riders, Monks and heavier unique units.
heavy-hei-guang-cavalry.tactics:
## Civilization differences
The three civilizations get different versions. Wei Heavy Hei Guang Cavalry have 30% more HP, +4 melee armor from Ming Guang Armor, +2 attack against siege from the Wei team bonus and a small food trickle from Tuntian. Wu ones get +2 attack from their civilization bonus and move 15% faster near Sun Jian. Shu ones regenerate near Liu Bei and are the only ones with Heresy. Bloodlines, the Blacksmith cavalry upgrades and Husbandry apply to all three.

## What beats Heavy Hei Guang Cavalry
The usual answers to heavy cavalry: Halberdiers, Kamayuks, Heavy Camel Riders, Mamelukes, Genoese Crossbowmen and Monks. Strong melee units such as Boyars, Teutonic Knights, Berserks, War Elephants and Elite Battle Elephants also beat them.

heavy-rocket-cart.description:
A gunpowder siege weapon upgraded from the Rocket Cart at the Siege Workshop in the Imperial Age for 800 wood and 600 gold. It replaces the Onager for the Chinese, Jurchens, Khitans and Koreans. It costs 135 wood and 155 gold and has 65 HP, 0/8 armor, a range of 8 and a minimum range of 2.5. Each volley fires 10 rockets that deal area damage and ignore the armor of non-siege land units. It can attack ground and destroy trees.

It is strong against tightly packed groups and moderately good against buildings. Units that reach it at close range, especially Condottieri and Winged Hussars, beat it.
heavy-rocket-cart.tactics:
## Compared with the Onager
The Heavy Rocket Cart fills the Onager's role. Its armor-ignoring rockets make it notably better against groups of armored units. The same reliance on many weak hits makes it worse against buildings with Masonry and Architecture, since building armor reduces every rocket and the armor-ignoring effect does not apply to buildings. It reloads faster, so how it compares depends heavily on the target's armor. It also has +5 HP, +1 pierce armor, faster training and a shorter minimum range than the Onager. Its HP sits halfway between the Onager and the Siege Onager, its pierce armor matches the Siege Onager's, and its other stats fall well short.

## Civilization differences
Every civilization with the unit has its own version, and all except the Khitans have an Imperial Age unique technology for it. Chinese Rocketry adds 25% attack, and Jurchen Thunderclap Bombs makes rockets detonate after landing and the cart explode when destroyed. Korean Heavy Rocket Carts with Shinkichon are the strongest, with 10 range, extra rockets and the most damage, which makes them a solid counter to enemy Onagers. Siege Engineers adds range and damage against buildings.

## What beats Heavy Rocket Carts
Units that get inside the minimum range. Its gunpowder armor class makes Condottieri and Winged Hussars the main threats.

hei-guang-cavalry.description:
A heavy cavalry unit of the Shu, Wei and Wu, trained at the Stable from the Castle Age in place of the Knight line. It upgrades to the Heavy Hei Guang Cavalry in the Imperial Age for 350 food and 250 gold.

Compared with the Knight it costs 65 food and 65 gold instead of 60 and 75, trains in 28 seconds instead of 30, and has 11 attack and 4/3 armor against 10 and 2/2. Its weak point is HP: 60 against the Knight's 100. The high armor keeps it alive longer than that number suggests, but anti-cavalry units with big bonuses cut through it.
hei-guang-cavalry.tactics:
## Armor over hit points
The Hei Guang Cavalry trades HP for armor, so it survives longer than expected against many opponents, and it does well against infantry, siege weapons and light cavalry. Elite Skirmishers are an exception: they deal 1 damage per hit to both the Hei Guang and the Knight, and the Hei Guang has far fewer HP to absorb it. The three civilizations have slightly different versions. Wei Hei Guang Cavalry have the most HP and +2 attack against siege, and Wu ones gain +2 attack in the Imperial Age.

## What beats Hei Guang Cavalry
Anti-cavalry units with high bonus damage, such as Pikemen, Kamayuks, Camel Riders and Mamelukes. Against them the low HP is a liability, making the Hei Guang almost as weak as Light Cavalry and considerably worse than a Knight. Heavy melee units such as Boyars, Teutonic Knights, Berserks and War and Battle Elephants also beat it, as do Genoese Crossbowmen. Monks can convert it.

houfnice.description:
The second Bohemian unique unit, a long-range gunpowder siege weapon that replaces the Bombard Cannon. It is unlocked at the Siege Workshop in the Imperial Age, needs Chemistry, and costs 225 wood and 225 gold. As a final upgrade it has no Elite version.

The Houfnice has 12 range and big bonuses against buildings, ships, stone defenses and siege, with a slightly larger blast than a Bombard Cannon. It is tougher than the cannon it replaces and wins the trade against Siege Onagers. Like other siege it is slow and has a minimum range of 5, so fast melee units that reach it destroy it.
houfnice.tactics:
## What the upgrade buys
Compared to a Bombard Cannon, the Houfnice has 10 more HP, 1 more pierce armor, 10 more attack, a 0.2 tile larger blast radius, +10 more bonus damage against ships, stone defenses and heavy siege, and +50 more against buildings. The upgrade costs 1,100 food and 800 gold, which pays off faster than it seems since Bombard Cannons are already expensive. Siege Engineers adds 1 range and 20% damage against buildings, and Wagenburg Tactics makes it 15% faster.

## Durability and anti-siege
A Houfnice takes 23 fully upgraded Arbalester bolts to kill, where a Bombard Cannon takes 16, and fully upgraded Elite Skirmishers deal only 1 damage to it. Its larger blast radius makes it more effective against massed infantry and foot archers. Against Siege Onagers the usual trade flips: a Siege Onager needs two shots to kill a Houfnice, while one Houfnice shot kills a Siege Onager (guaranteed with attack ground). It also does well against slow units, ships and other siege.

## What beats Houfnices
Melee units that get inside its minimum range, especially fast ones such as Condottieri, Elite Eagle Warriors and Magyar Huszars. Mangudai are also listed as a counter. Because of its slow speed it needs other units to screen it from raids.

ibirapema-warrior.description:
The second Tupi unique unit, a durable infantry soldier trained at the Barracks from the Castle Age and upgraded to Elite Ibirapema Warrior in the Imperial Age. It costs 30 food and 60 gold and has 80 HP, 8 attack and 2/1 armor. Its two-handed sweep deals full damage to every enemy in a cone in front of it, much like the Ghulam's attack but at 100% instead of 50%.

It returns 15% of its cost when killed. It is the Tupi melee front line and beats dense groups of infantry and low armored cavalry. The high gold cost makes it hard to mass late, and archers and heavily armored melee units beat it.
ibirapema-warrior.tactics:
## Using Ibirapema Warriors
The low food cost helps in the Castle Age, and the Elite upgrade costs 50% less food, so it can be taken quickly in the early Imperial Age. In mass battles Ibirapema Warriors beat the Militia line and unique infantry with low melee armor, such as Huskarls, Ghulams, Shotel Warriors and Karambit Warriors, by a wide margin. They also do well against groups of low armored cavalry that stand in front of them. Their damage against buildings is lower than other infantry, and Blast Furnace is not available to them. Tupi Champi Warriors with Caciques and foot archers with Curare cover most of their weaknesses.

## What beats Ibirapema Warriors
Archers, Hand Cannoneers above all, because of the low pierce armor, though the sweep does heavy damage if they reach a clump of ranged units. Teutonic Knights, Samurai, Jaguar Warriors, Obuchs, Urumi Swordsmen, Legionaries and Liao Dao beat them cost effectively, and all cost less gold. Cataphracts, especially with Logistica, and War and Battle Elephants are even more effective. Chakram Throwers, Scorpions and Organ Guns also beat them.

iron-pagoda.description:
The Iron Pagoda is the unique unit of the Jurchens, a heavy cavalry unit trained at the Castle from the Castle Age. The Jurchens have no Knight line, so it fills that role for them. It costs 80 food and 55 gold, trains in 14 seconds and has 115 HP, 12 attack, 1/3 armor and a speed of 1.4. Once every 40 seconds it completely blocks one melee attack. The Elite Iron Pagoda in the Imperial Age has 140 HP, 13 attack and 2/3 armor, and its block recharges every 30 seconds.

It beats infantry, archers, siege weapons and light cavalry, and loses to the usual anti-cavalry units.
iron-pagoda.tactics:
## Heavy cavalry from the Castle
At 14 seconds per unit, one Castle producing Iron Pagodas turns out more units than two Stables producing Knights. They cost the same total as a Knight but lean much more on food, which together with the Castle requirement makes them tricky to sustain in the early Castle Age and much easier later on. In the Castle Age they compare to the Cavalier, with one more point of line of sight and pierce armor, one less melee armor and slightly more speed. The Elite Iron Pagoda has 20 HP and 1 attack less than a Paladin, but it is faster and its upgrade is cheaper and much quicker to research.

## The block
The block works like extra HP equal to the blocked hit, which helps against high-damage units, or like getting one attack in first, which helps against low-HP units. It recharges slowly and affects only one blow per fight, so it wins close melee fights without changing hard counters. It negates the blast of suicide units such as Flaming Camels and Demolition Ships, but it does not stop charged special attacks or any projectile.

## Support
Spearmen or Fire Lancers help against Camel Riders and stronger cavalry, while Grenadiers and Rocket Carts handle infantry and Skirmishers, with the Jurchen bonus halving their friendly fire. The Jurchens' own Skirmishers deal with Spearmen and with archers such as Genoese Crossbowmen and Composite Bowmen.

## What beats Iron Pagodas
Mamelukes are a hard counter, since their ranged melee attack gets past both the block and the pierce armor. Heavy Camel Riders, Pikemen, Kamayuks, Genoese Crossbowmen, Boyars, Berserks, Teutonic Knights and elephants also beat them. Monks are a serious threat because the Jurchens lack both Faith and Heresy.

jian-swordsman.description:
The Jian Swordsman is the second unique unit of the Wu, a shock infantry unit trained at the Barracks from the Castle Age. It has no Elite upgrade. It costs 45 food and 50 gold and trains in 35 seconds.

When its HP drops below 45 it drops its shield, losing 3 pierce armor but gaining 3 attack and 10% speed, and it switches back once healed above 45. The Wu regeneration bonus heals it over time. With 5 pierce armor and +4 against archers it is a strong anti-archer unit. Its shock infantry class makes it very weak to swordsmen and other infantry with bonuses against that class.
jian-swordsman.tactics:
## Using Jian Swordsmen
Jian Swordsmen work like enhanced Eagle Warriors and compete with Huskarls as the Wu answer to archers, arguably doing better thanks to regeneration. Their base pierce armor is the second highest among infantry. With Scale Mail Armor they reach 6 pierce armor, so Crossbowmen deal 1 damage per shot, and with Chain Mail Armor Cavalry Archers do the same. That makes an early Castle Age raid on an enemy town very damaging, though the long training time makes them slow to mass.

They tend to lose even fights against melee cavalry, so pair them with Wu Pikemen, which also regenerate. Sun Jian nearby gives them 15% more speed.

## What beats Jian Swordsmen
Long Swordsmen and Champions, because of the shock infantry class, along with many unique infantry units. Samurai and Jaguar Warriors are the worst matchups: both have bonuses against shock infantry, and Samurai also hit unique units hard while Jaguar Warriors also hit infantry hard. Ranged infantry with bonuses against shock infantry get the first hit and can kite them. Hand Cannoneers punch through the pierce armor and kill one in four shots, and Slingers and Grenadiers are very effective for the same reason. Heavy cavalry, especially Cataphracts, also beat them.

kona.description:
The Mapuche unique cavalry, trained at the Castle from the Castle Age, with an Elite upgrade in the Imperial Age. It costs 65 food and 40 gold, trains in 14 seconds and has 125 HP (145 as Elite), 9 attack (11 as Elite), no melee armor, 3 pierce armor (5 as Elite) and +5 against gunpowder units. It gains +1 attack for every 15% of HP its target has already lost, up to +6.

It is a fast glass cannon that does well against gunpowder units and low armor units. The Mapuche lack cavalry armor upgrades, so heavily armored melee units, Pikemen and Camel Riders beat it.
kona.tactics:
## Using the ability
The bonus counts any damage the target has taken, including damage from other units. Pair them with ranged units such as the Bolas Rider, especially after Malon: the ranged units soften targets first and the Konas finish them with the extra attack. Use both for raids, since the Mapuche earn 3 gold for every military unit they kill. Against low armor units every hit lowers the target's HP and raises the Kona's damage, so they snowball. Against Fire Lancers the result depends on numbers, resources and civilization, since both deal heavy damage to each other at a similar cost.

The Kona is balanced around having no cavalry upgrades. The Mapuche only need the Forging line and later the Elite upgrade, while other civilizations pay for Bloodlines, Husbandry and armor, but the Kona ends up with far lower armor in the late game. After Butalmapu it costs 15% less and becomes one of the most cost-effective cavalry units in the game, able to beat Paladins and even Relic-boosted Leiciai for equal resources.

## What beats Konas
Units with high melee armor, because the Kona's attack and attack speed start low: Teutonic Knights, Boyars, Serjeants and Monaspas. Iron Pagodas block melee hits with their shield. Pikemen and Camel Riders still defeat them, and large groups of ranged units punish their unupgraded pierce armor. Danish and Khitan infantry reflect the extra damage with Hamask and Lamellar Armor. Monks and other healers undo the ability by healing injured units. Samurai, elephants and Genoese Crossbowmen also beat them.

legionary.description:
The Roman unique infantry unit, a unique upgrade of the Long Swordsman at the Barracks in the Imperial Age that replaces the Two-Handed Swordsman and the Champion. It has no Elite upgrade. The upgrade costs 800 food and 400 gold, which saves 50 food, 50 gold and 15 seconds of research compared with the two Champion line upgrades together.

It costs 50 food and 20 gold and has 75 HP, 12 attack and 2/2 armor, with bonuses against infantry, shock infantry and buildings. It beats trash units and most infantry, but it is slow and only moderately tough, so archers, heavy cavalry and splash damage siege beat it.
legionary.tactics:
## Compared with the Champion
Fully upgraded, a Legionary has 2 more melee armor (6, like the Teutons), 5 more HP and +4 against infantry, but 2 less attack than a Champion, and the Romans lack Arson. The Romans get double effect from Blacksmith armor technologies, so missing either the upgrade or Plate Mail Armor early in the Imperial Age does little harm. Comitatenses makes Legionaries train 50% faster and gives them a charge attack of +5 over 20 seconds. Centurions boost their speed and rate of fire, and Heavy Scorpions help against archers and infantry.

## Where Legionaries shine
They are strongest in the early Imperial Age, when their counters are less common, and in the late Imperial Age when gold runs short. They easily beat Halberdiers, Elite Skirmishers and Hussars, though Genitours and Magyar Huszars give them more trouble. The infantry bonus makes them very good against Berserks, Kamayuks and Woad Raiders, and Samurai do not counter them because they upgrade from a common unit.

## What beats Legionaries
Archers, Heavy Scorpions and Onagers, since Legionaries are slow and have modest HP. Heavy cavalry such as Paladins, Boyars, Cataphracts and elephants also beat them. Jaguar Warriors and Teutonic Knights have stronger stats, and Liao Dao win through bleeding damage unless a Centurion is boosting the Legionaries. Champions from strong infantry civilizations, such as Armenians with Fereters, Dravidians with Wootz Steel, Japanese and Slavs with Druzhina, are hard fights too, though a nearby Centurion lets the Legionary hold its own.

liao-dao.description:
The first Khitan unique unit, a heavy infantry unit trained at the Castle in the Castle Age for 40 food and 40 gold. It can be upgraded to Elite Liao Dao in the Imperial Age. Each hit also wounds the target, dealing 9 extra damage over 3 seconds that ignores armor and stacks. Siege weapons, ships and buildings do not bleed.

With solid HP, 3 melee armor and the bleed, the Liao Dao is a very dangerous melee fighter against both infantry and cavalry. Its pierce armor is low and it attacks slowly, so archers, ranged siege and Monks beat it, and it costs more than most unique infantry.
liao-dao.tactics:
## Winning melee fights
For equal resources the Liao Dao beats Jaguar Warriors and Teutonic Knights, and stronger cavalry unique units such as Boyars, Monaspas, Konniks and Leiciai without Relics. Samurai, Urumi Swordsmen, Legionaries with a Centurion and Comitatenses, and fully upgraded Cataphracts can narrowly win. With Lamellar Armor, which reflects 25% of melee damage, it also beats Battle Elephants, since part of the trample damage comes back to them. It still loses to War Elephants. Its anti-cavalry strength makes up for the Khitan lack of Halberdiers. The bleed also stops regenerating units such as Berserks, Berber camels and Wu infantry from healing properly. Khitan Forging and Iron Casting give it +2 attack each.

## Covering its weaknesses
The Liao Dao has less pierce armor than a Champion with Gambesons, which limits its raiding. Its 2.4 second attack is the slowest of any infantry outside the Spearman line, so it does worse against buildings than the Militia line. Faster-trained Khitan Elite Skirmishers, which also get Lamellar Armor, or Rocket Carts pair well with it. Siege Rams garrisoned with Liao Dao are dangerous, since the Liao Dao protect the rams better than other infantry.

## What beats Liao Dao
Arbalesters, Hand Cannoneers and Cavalry Archers shoot them down, though a Liao Dao that reaches archers does heavy damage with its bonus against them. Mangonels, Scorpions, Chakram Throwers and Gbetos also deal with them if protected, and siege takes no bleed damage. Monks can convert them, and Samurai and War Elephants beat them in melee.

lou-chuan.description:
A regional siege ship trained at the Dock in the Imperial Age by the Chinese, Jurchens, Shu, Wei and Wu, in place of the Cannon Galleon. It costs 250 wood and 225 gold and has 175 HP and 0/9 armor. A Traction Trebuchet on the prow throws rocks at buildings and siege from range 13, and a tower fires ten arrows at other units from range 10.

It switches between the two attacks on its own, and missed shots still deal full damage. That makes it far more versatile than the Cannon Galleon and better against buildings than even an Elite Cannon Galleon. It costs a lot of gold and is weak to Fire Ships.
lou-chuan.tactics:
## Attack modes
The trebuchet attack is used against buildings, mechanical siege and for attack ground. It benefits from Siege Engineers but not from Ballistics or the Fletching line. The arrows are used against all other units, including organic siege such as the Armored Elephant line and Ballista Elephants, and benefit from the Fletching line and Ballistics. Attack ground fires only rocks. The Chinese can research Rocketry, which turns the arrows into rockets with splash damage. Jurchen Thunderclap Bombs adds grenades from the trebuchet against units, and Lou Chuans then explode when destroyed. Shu Bolt Magazine adds three more arrows, and Wu Sitting Tiger adds two extra rocks.

## Lou Chuan, Cannon Galleon or Dromon
Its faster reload makes it better at destroying buildings than an Elite Cannon Galleon, at a much higher gold cost. Compared to the Dromon it is far stronger against buildings and far weaker against units.

## What beats Lou Chuans
Fire Ships of the Fire Galley line. The Lou Chuan also has a minimum range of 3, so it cannot shoot at ships that get right next to it.

mounted-trebuchet.description:
The Mounted Trebuchet is the second unique unit of the Khitans, a camel-mounted siege unit trained at the Siege Workshop from the Imperial Age. It costs 175 food and 175 gold and has 75 HP, 30 attack, a range of 10 with a minimum range of 3, and 2/4 armor. It has no Elite upgrade and needs no Chemistry.

Each shot leaves a patch of fire for 10 seconds that damages enemy units and buildings and ignores armor. Despite the name it works like a Bombard Cannon and attacks units before buildings. It is strong against other siege weapons and weak against buildings.
mounted-trebuchet.tactics:
## An alternative to the Bombard Cannon
Mounted Trebuchets suit fighting units better than buildings, since they cannot outrange Castles and have little bonus damage against buildings. The blast, the lingering fire and reasonable mobility make them effective against other siege units. Because they need no Chemistry, they give the Khitans a major advantage early in the Imperial Age as a way to push back enemy siege from a safe distance. They cost food instead of wood, so production can become a bottleneck for smaller economies.

## Durability
They count as heavy siege, so a single shot from an enemy Bombard Cannon or Onager can knock them out. They move faster than a Bombard Cannon, which makes them easier to micromanage out of the way. Cavalry armor technologies raise their melee armor to 5 and make it hard for enemy archers to bring them down. That melee armor helps most against weaker units such as Hussars and Karambit Warriors.

## What beats Mounted Trebuchets
Enemy Bombard Cannons and Onagers, which can knock them out with one hit. Mangudai beat them thanks to their attack bonus, unlike other archers. Heavy Camel Riders, Halberdiers and Magyar Huszars kill them easily with bonus damage, and Paladins and Champions do the same with their high base attack.

rocket-cart.description:
The Rocket Cart is a gunpowder siege weapon trained at the Siege Workshop from the Castle Age. It replaces the Mangonel for the Chinese, Jurchens, Khitans and Koreans, and upgrades to the Heavy Rocket Cart in the Imperial Age. Each volley fires 8 rockets into the target area for area damage, and the attacks ignore the armor of non-siege land units.

It costs 135 wood and 155 gold and has 45 HP, a range of 7 and a minimum range of 2.5. Like the Mangonel it is good against tightly packed groups and fairly good against buildings. It is helpless against units that get close, and its gunpowder class draws extra damage from some units.
rocket-cart.tactics:
## Compared with the Mangonel
Rocket Carts deal notably more damage than Mangonels to groups of armored units, because their attacks bypass armor, and they fire a little faster. Relying on many weak rockets makes them worse against buildings with Masonry, which cancels part of the building bonus for every projectile, and the armor bypass does not work on buildings. They also have 5 fewer HP, train 15% faster, have a shorter minimum range, and their upgrade costs more in total but uses wood instead of food.

## Civilization differences
In the Castle Age the one notable difference is for the Jurchens, who get Siege Engineers early and extra line of sight. The +1 range lets their Rocket Carts outrange every generic archer with Bodkin Arrow and every siege unit of that Age. Only Khmer-allied Scorpions, Briton foot archers and Aztec and Briton Skirmishers can match it. Chinese Rocket Carts get +25% attack from Rocketry, Korean ones get extra range and rockets from Shinkichon, and Jurchen rockets detonate after landing with Thunderclap Bombs.

## What beats Rocket Carts
Units that get in close, inside the minimum range where the cart cannot fire. Condottieri and Winged Hussars are major threats because they have bonus damage against the gunpowder class.

savar.description:
The Persian unique heavy cavalry, an upgrade of the Cavalier at the Stable in the Imperial Age that replaces the Paladin. The upgrade costs 1,200 food and 600 gold and takes 160 seconds, cheaper and faster than the Paladin. A Savar costs 60 food and 75 gold and has 145 HP, 14 attack and 3/4 armor, with +4 attack against archers including the Persian team bonus.

It is one of the strongest units in the game and dominates infantry, archers, siege and unprepared towns. The standard anti-cavalry units still beat it, and Monks are a threat because the Persians lack Heresy.
savar.tactics:
## Savar compared with the Paladin
Over the Cavalier, the Savar has +25 HP, +2 attack and +1/+2 armor. Compared with the Paladin it gives up 15 HP for +1/+1 armor, +2 attack against archers and a faster attack, as fast as the Cavalier. A fully upgraded Savar kills Arbalesters without Ring Archer Armor in two hits instead of three and takes 83 Arbalester shots instead of 60, so it handles archers much better. It also beats a Paladin one on one thanks to the attack speed, though Frankish, Teutonic and Lithuanian Paladins with 3 or 4 Relics still win. The higher armor makes it more durable against most ranged units and many melee ones. Units dealing heavy single hits, units that ignore armor and trample damage from elephants and similar sources hurt it more than a Paladin.

## Using Savars
A large group can destroy any ill-prepared town or army. Siege weapons rarely work against them, although carefully used Onagers can deal a lot of damage. Use them with care, because losing them is very costly.

## What beats Savars
Halberdiers lose one on one but win easily on cost, and Heavy Camel Riders beat them on both cost and population. Monks are dangerous since Savars cost a lot of gold and the Persians lack Heresy. Genoese Crossbowmen with their anti-cavalry bonus, Composite Bowmen that ignore pierce armor and Bolas Riders with bonus damage and a snare are major threats. Elite Battle Elephants, War Elephants, Boyars, Kamayuks, Berserks, Teutonic Knights and Mamelukes also beat them.

temple-guard.description:
The second Muisca unique unit, a powerful shock infantry unit trained at the Barracks or the Monastery from the Castle Age. The Elite Temple Guard upgrade costs 500 food and 650 gold and is researched in the Imperial Age at the Barracks only. It costs 70 food and 45 gold.

It has 100 HP and 11 attack with bonuses against cavalry, camels and elephants, so it sits between the Militia line and the Spearman line in role. Each hit shortens its reload time for 5 seconds, so it attacks faster the longer a fight lasts. Heavy infantry, archers and Cataphracts beat it.
temple-guard.tactics:
## Rising attack speed
Every hit lowers the reload time by 0.2 seconds for 5 seconds, down to a minimum of 1 second, and the cycle settles after about 14.6 seconds of fighting. This makes Temple Guards effective against units with high HP or high melee armor, such as elephants, Boyars and Paladins, and very good against buildings, helped by rams or Siege Towers to get close to Castles and Town Centers. They also beat trash units and other shock infantry, and with the right positioning they handle rams, Trebuchets, Bombard Cannons and Onagers, though masses of Scorpions should be avoided.

## Muisca compositions
With no Halberdier and no Blast Furnace, the Muisca use the Temple Guard as their main cavalry counter. Support it with Slingers against infantry and Guecha Warriors, Champi Warriors or Skirmishers against archers. Training them at a Monastery helps protect Relics. A Temple Guard rush can follow a Feudal Champi rush, or come from a Fast Castle with many Monasteries, mixing in Monks to heal and convert.

## What beats Temple Guards
Heavy infantry, since Temple Guards are shock infantry. Danish and Khitan infantry are notable threats because Hamask and Lamellar Armor turn the rising damage against them. Archers punish their average speed, and mounted archers and Hand Cannoneers especially, though high HP and pierce armor help against Arbalesters. Cataphracts cancel their cavalry bonus and beat them decisively, especially with Logistica, and Konniks are another exception because they turn into their dismounted forms.

tiger-cavalry.description:
The Wei unique unit, a heavy cavalry unit trained at the Castle in the Castle Age for 60 food and 80 gold. It can be upgraded to Elite Tiger Cavalry in the Imperial Age. For each of its first four kills it gains +10 HP and +1 attack, up to +40 HP and +4 attack.

Tiger Cavalry excel against archers thanks to their speed, 4 pierce armor (5 for Elite) and a large bonus against archers. They also deal bonus damage to siege. They have no melee armor, so in melee they are only decent, and Pikemen, Camel Riders and stronger melee units beat them.
tiger-cavalry.tactics:
## Hunting archers
After one kill a Tiger Cavalry kills generic Elite Skirmishers and Crossbowmen in two hits, and an Elite Tiger Cavalry kills Arbalesters and Hand Cannoneers in two hits, where a Paladin needs three. Without kills it takes 49 Arbalester shots to die against a Paladin's 60, and it needs at least three kills to match the Paladin's durability. Genoese Crossbowmen and Composite Bowmen are still a threat once massed. The higher gold cost than Knights makes them harder to mass in long 1v1 games, while in team games trade can cover it.

## Compositions
Monks pair well because healing preserves the gains from kills, but the Wei lack Heresy, so Tiger Cavalry are open to conversion themselves.
