Elite Skirmishers or Xianbei Raiders handle Halberdiers, and Halberdiers handle Camel Riders. Heavy Hei Guang Cavalry with Ming Guang Armor covers the melee weakness, while the Tiger Cavalry soaks ranged damage. Cao Cao nearby adds 10% attack speed.

## What beats Tiger Cavalry
Pikemen, Kamayuks and Camel Riders, made worse by the lack of melee armor. Without kills a Tiger Cavalry loses to a Knight one on one, and it loses to Paladins and to Cavaliers with strong bonuses, such as Malian or Bulgarian ones. Boyars, Leiciai, Konniks and Monaspas beat it for equal numbers and resources, as do War and Battle Elephants. Konas are a major threat without Ming Guang Armor. Jaguar Warriors, Teutonic Knights, Samurai and Liao Dao win in melee, and Monks, Mamelukes and Berserks also counter it.

traction-trebuchet.description:
A regional siege weapon for the Three Kingdoms civilizations, Shu, Wei and Wu, built at the Siege Workshop in the Imperial Age. It replaces both the Trebuchet and the Bombard Cannon for them. It costs 175 wood and 210 gold and has 115 HP, range 14, a minimum range of 4 and 230 attack against buildings.

It does not need to pack or unpack and fires at enemy units in range on its own, preferring units over buildings. It deals no splash damage and can attack the ground and cut down trees. With only 8 pierce armor and a speed of 0.57, it is slow and fragile, and Monks can convert it from a distance.
traction-trebuchet.tactics:
## Using Traction Trebuchets
This is the only long range anti-building siege the Three Kingdoms civilizations have. Since it never packs up, it is more practical than a Trebuchet for hitting units, and with good micro it can even kite slower units. Hero auras do not affect it.

## Differences between civilizations
Shu Traction Trebuchets move faster, which helps them retreat and reposition, and Shu is the only one of the three with Siege Engineers and Heresy, giving more range and damage against buildings. Wei Traction Trebuchets are cheaper, which makes them the easiest long range siege in the game to mass, though they lack Siege Engineers and Heresy. Wu has Sitting Tiger, which adds two projectiles with extra damage and better area coverage, so Wu Traction Trebuchets are the most useful for supporting an army against masses of units.

## What beats Traction Trebuchets
Melee units that close the gap before the minimum range stops the trebuchet from firing, especially Magyar Huszars and Elite Eagle Warriors. Rams, Bombard Cannons, Mangudai and Onagers beat it too, and its low pierce armor leaves it far more exposed to arrows than a regular Trebuchet. Monks can convert it from range.

varangian-guard.description:
The Varangian Guard is a regional infantry unit of the Byzantines, Danes, Saxons, Varangians and Vikings, trained at the Barracks from the Castle Age. It costs 65 food and 45 gold and has 70 HP, 13 attack, 2/1 armor and a speed of 1.05. While attacking enemy units it generates 35 gold per minute. It upgrades to the Elite Varangian Guard in the Imperial Age for 750 food and 475 gold.

It is a generalist frontline fighter that trades well with most units. It counts as shock infantry, so Champions and other infantry with bonus damage beat it, and it is poor against buildings.
varangian-guard.tactics:
## A heavy frontline
Varangian Guards are straightforward heavy infantry that trade efficiently with most units, helped by the gold they earn while fighting. They fill broadly the same role as the Militia line and cost more per unit, but have stronger stats, including higher melee armor and better speed. They also need fewer technologies to reach full strength, which makes the transition faster. They trade very well against Halberdiers, act as a soft counter to melee cavalry and are slightly less vulnerable to archers than the Champion.

## Not for razing
The gold only comes from fighting units, never from attacking buildings, and they lack the Militia line's bonus against buildings. For razing enemy towns the Militia line is always the better choice.

## Civilization differences
Saxon Varangian Guards cost up to 20% less with enough Castles and Town Centers. Danish ones move faster and loot part of a building's cost when they destroy it. Varangian ones attack faster and generate 50% more gold, and Viking ones have more HP and bonus damage against cavalry and camels but one less pierce armor.

## What beats Varangian Guards
Champions and many unique melee infantry units, which deal bonus damage to shock infantry. Hand Cannoneers and Slingers shred them, and mounted archers can kite them. Unique cavalry such as Boyars, Cataphracts, Konniks, Monaspas and Leitis defeats them cost-effectively.

white-feather-guard.description:
The White Feather Guard is the Shu unique unit, an anti-cavalry infantry unit trained at the Castle from the Castle Age and upgraded to Elite White Feather Guard in the Imperial Age. It costs 60 food and 15 gold and trains in 11 seconds.

It has 95 HP, +8 attack against cavalry and elephants and a bonus against shock infantry, and every hit slows non-siege enemies by 15% for 10 seconds. It is cheap and durable, but its base damage is low because the Shu lack Iron Casting and Blast Furnace. Ranged units, heavy infantry and some heavy cavalry beat it.
white-feather-guard.tactics:
## Using White Feather Guards
White Feather Guards are cheap defensive infantry that protect Shu archers and War Chariots from cavalry. The slow keeps enemies from reaching your ranged units, and each new hit from any White Feather Guard resets its timer. Decent pierce armor and the extra HP from Coiled Serpent Array, which grows with the number of Spearmen and White Feather Guards nearby, let them take a fair number of arrows. That also makes them durable raiders in enemy towns. Near Liu Bei they heal 45 HP per minute.

## What beats White Feather Guards
They move slowly, so ranged units still work against them, especially Hand Cannoneers, Slingers and Grenadiers, along with foot archers and mounted archers. Champions and many unique infantry units beat them with or without Coiled Serpent Array, though shock infantry do poorly against them. Some cavalry also win: Cataphracts cancel the anti-cavalry bonus, War Elephants have the HP and trample damage, Boyars have enough melee armor to shrug off the low base attack, and Konniks counter them completely once dismounted.

xianbei-raider.description:
The second Wei unique unit, a mounted archer trained at the Archery Range from the Castle Age that replaces the Cavalry Archer line. It has no Elite upgrade. It costs 65 wood and 35 gold, trains in 29 seconds and has 36 HP in the Castle Age (40 in the Imperial Age), 5 attack, a range of 4 and bonuses against Spearmen and infantry. A charged volley fires five extra arrows and recharges over 30 seconds.

It is weak in HP and attack but cheap in gold and easy to keep alive. It does well against slow melee units, Spearmen and Monks, while Skirmishers, Genitours and Camel Riders beat it.
xianbei-raider.tactics:
## Using Xianbei Raiders
The Xianbei Raider has about the HP of an Archer and the attack of a Crossbowman, so it does not compare directly with the Cavalry Archer. Its extra bonus against infantry and the charged volley make up for this: the volley arrows always hit for full damage, and against Spearmen they deal about 30 damage before Parthian Tactics. It attacks 11.1% faster than an Archer, and Cao Cao nearby raises that. Its main drawback is a long attack delay, slightly worse than the Cavalry Archer's.

Its low gold cost makes it very affordable in the late game, and it trains in about the time of a Crossbowman. Ming Guang Armor takes its melee armor up to 8, which makes it durable against low-attack units such as Hussars or Karambit Warriors, though its low HP leaves it exposed to bonus damage. With hit and run it does acceptably against cavalry, but Paladins, Savars and Tiger Cavalry are too much for it. Monks do poorly against it: it is cheap, the volley snipes them quickly, and one converted Raider is not worth much.

## What beats Xianbei Raiders
Elite Skirmishers and Genitours hard counter them, and Camel Riders and Elephant Archers are deadly. Genoese Crossbowmen, Bolas Riders, Camel Archers and Mamelukes deal bonus damage to them, and Rattan Archers have high pierce armor. Huskarls, Ghulams and Elite Eagle Warriors give them some trouble. The volley is not used against siege, so they are poor against Mangonels, Scorpions and rams, and defensive structures beat them as well.
